This interpretation of saddhā finds its rationale from a study of the nature of saddhā as motivating spiritual activities (pakkhandanarasā) and clarifying (pasādanarasā) mind behind Buddhist religious practice. Moreover, the interaction of faith in its cognitive mode and faith in its affective mode also confirms this interpretation. Without faith in its affective mode, a positive emotional response to someone or something one has heard or read, faith in its cognitive mode, putative knowledge or awareness that amounts to belief in propositions or statements of which one does not, or cannot, have direct knowledge, is not possible. Therefore, faith and its devotional and ritual expression in Buddhism constitute a preliminary meditative practice, settling and composing the mind in preparation for the higher stages of Buddhist meditative practice.

articles.title_kr: 빠알리어 접미사 tūna, tvāna, tvā에 관한 연구 __『깟짜야나 문법』, 『목갈라나 문법』, 『삿다니띠』를 중심으로__
articles.title_en: A Study on Pāli Suffixes tūna, tvāna, tvā with reference to Kaccāyana-vyākaraṇa, Moggallāna-vyākaraṇa, Saddanīti
articles.abstract_kr: Words with the suffixes, ~tūna, ~tvāna, ~tvā often appears in Pāli Canon and western scholars have called them gerund, indeclinable (past) participle, or absolutive. This paper aims to study the abbreviation, grammatical category, function, and substitution of these Pāli suffixes, namely, tūna, tvāna, tvā, focused on the relevant rules of Kaccāyana-vyākaraṇa(KV), Moggallāna-vyākaraṇa(MV), Saddanīti(Sadd).The suffixes tūna, tvāna, tvā in three grammar texts are abbreviated to tūnādayo(tūna etc.), tūnādayo belongs to kita, a class of suffixes that are applied directly to the verbal root to form primary derivatives. These derivatives are indeclinables that do not belong to the category of ‘noun’ that is declinable.The main function of tūnādayo is to express the preceding action in time. Out of two or more actions performed by one doer, tūnādayo are applied after the verbal root denoting the preceding action, and the words with this suffix are mainly translated into ‘having done’ and ‘after doing’. With regard to the secondary functions, the suffixes are used to denote the concurrent action of one doer, the future action than the main verb, the preceding action of different doers, or cause, but the frequency of use is low. And those suffixes are sometimes substituted by ya, acca, svāna, svā, mma, yha, jja, bbha, and ddha in some cases.With regard to the grammatical rules related to the subject of this study, KV presents main function along with various examples, MV uses questions and answers to enable a good understanding of the function of rules, and Sadd specifically presents various ranges of use, therefore it was possible to examine tūnādayo in various ways of the three grammar texts.As the final process of this study, both suitability and fallacy of the modern term of words ending in tūnādayo were examined, through this process, the grammatical range and feature of words ending in tūnādayo became manifest. And one thing is clear that the suffix-centered description in KV, MV, Sadd regarding the grammatical topics such as tūnādayo are more accessible than to try to correspond to existing English or Korean grammatical categories.

articles.title_kr: 중관학파와 나스띠까 붓다빨리따, 바비베까, 짠드라끼르띠의 허무주의 논란에 대한 해명 비교연구
articles.title_en: The Mādhyamikas and the Nāstikas A comparative review of Buddhapālita’s, Bhāviveka’s, and Candrakīrti’s responses to the charge of nihilism
articles.abstract_kr: This paper reviews and compares three commentators’ discussions on the outsider’s charge that the Mādhyamikas are similar to the nāstikas found in their commentaries on Nāgārjuna’s Mūlamadhyamakakārikā 18.7. Buddhapālita (5th cen.) expands the existing Mādhyamika response to the critique, while Bhāviveka (6th cen.), denouncing the traditional answer that acknowledges the outer similarities between the Mādhyamikas and the nāstikas, submits a new one framed according to the two truths. On the other hand, Candrakīrti (7th cen.) defended the traditional stance to the charge, though adopting new elements from Bhāviveka’s discussion.

articles.title_kr: 정토불교의 여성에 대한 인식과 구원론에 대한 고찰 __『무량수경(無量壽經)』 제35원을 중심으로__
articles.title_en: A Study on the Perception and Redemption of Women in Pure Land Buddhism: Centering on the 35th edition of the Sukhāvatīvyuha Sūtra
articles.abstract_kr: The scriptures are formed during the interaction between text and context. Such an interaction not only defines but also liberates human life.Based on the active interaction between text and context, this paper examines the view of women based on the human understanding and salvation theory of Pure Land Buddhism, which has a lot of influence to this day.The object of salvation seen in Pure Land Buddhism is universal. The door to salvation is open to everyone. However, the contents of the 35th among the 48 members of The Larger Sukhāvatīvyuha Sūtra unfolds as if there were restrictions on women in salvation. Starting with the question of whether women are the object of hatred and whether the Sect of Pure Land claims to be unfaithful to women, the original meaning is to be deduced by studying the Chinese and English versions reflecting each era of the 35th member.It is necessary to take a step further from the explanatory approach of reflecting the negative content of women in the scriptures. This is because the alienation or discriminatory content of women in the scriptures is not limited to the story or the past society, but is a accusation against the very general alienation that occurs frequently today and is applicable.Therefore, through the consideration of women in No. 35 of the The Larger Sukhāvatīvyuha Sūtra, we will seek a path to humanization that declares freedom and freedom for all marginalized people beyond sex in this society where violence and alienation are taken for granted.

articles.title_kr: 티벳불교의 바르도(bar do)와 시토(zhi khro) 의례
articles.title_en: Bar do and Zhi khro rituals in Tibetan Buddhism
articles.abstract_kr: In the West, the scholarly study of the Nyingma school of Tibetan Buddhism has a long history dating back to the early 20th century, with an initial focus on the philological and historical analysis of its complex literature and its transmission, and a later emphasis on rituals and practices. However, Korean Buddhologists have typically devoted themselves to Seon (Chan) and Korean Buddhism, paying little attention to Vajrayana Buddhism in general and the Nyingma school in particular. Therefore, the first goal of this article is to introduce the notion of bardo (intermediate state) and zhi khro (peaceful and wrathful deities) rituals to Korean academia. To do so, a textual contextualization within the 'Ancient Tantric Collections' (rnying ma rgyud 'bum) is first presented, along with its related texts, and contemporary studies. This will allow us to examine the characteristics of the intermediate state in Tibetan Buddhism through the text The Great Liberation through Listening in the Bardo State (bar do thos grol chen mo), also known as The Tibetan Book of the Dead, and then, address the concept of “zhi khro,” which refers to esoterically described peaceful and wrathful deities and their rituals and which is somewhat unfamiliar to the Korean Buddhist.The paper shows how the intermediate state (bar do) and zhi khro rituals are concepts and practices that originated in the Guhyagarbha Tantra (rgyud gsang ba'i snying po, *密續秘密藏) in the Ancient Tantric Collections (rnying ma rgyud 'bum, 古密敎全集) and were further elaborated as Tibetan Buddhism developed. The iconography and symbolism of the 100 peaceful and wrathful deities in the Guhyagarbha Tantra were later further refined in Tibetan texts on the peaceful deities (zhi ba'i lha) and wrathful deities (khro bo'i lha), within which, the famous The Great Liberation through Listening in the Bardo State (bar do thos grol chen mo, 14C) is located.An innovative contribution of this article is the interpretation of the unique view of the intermediate state of Tibetan Buddhism as transmitted in the ancient translation school (rnying ma) through the Six Bardo Verses (drug gi rtsa tshig) from the Great Liberation through Listening in the Bardo State in order to discover the differences with the East Asian concept of the intermediate state contained in Zhong-yin (中陰), a representative Chinese translation of the intermediate state.By furthering the understanding of the Nyingma school of Tibetan Buddhism and introducing bardo and zhi khro rituals, we are able to situate Tibetan Buddhist practice in its historical and literary contexts, as well as its uniqueness and philosophical depth. This article shows the complexities of and rationale of these specific Tibetan Buddhist rituals and practices. In terms of practice, their essence is one, which to serve as skillful means, a method anyone can actually apply at all different states.

articles.title_kr: 반야중관학의 변증적 파기와 마조의 심(心)･불(佛)･도(道)
articles.title_en: Dialectical Destruction of Prajñā-Madhyamaka Studies(般若中觀學) and Mazu's the Mind(心), the Buddha(佛) and the Truth(道)
articles.abstract_kr: 본 연구는 ‘마조선이 인도사상의 색채를 벗어난 독자적으로 중국화된 선이라는 인식’과 ‘이러한 인식이 기반이 되어 해석된 야나기다 세이잔과 이리야 요시타카가 주장한 즉심즉불(卽心卽佛)이 평상심(平常心)과 가깝거나 같다는 인식’을 비판적으로 바라보면서, 반야중관학의 관점에서 마조의 “즉심즉불과 평상심시도”의 의미를 분석한 연구다. 용수의 사구분별적 변증논법과 삼론학의 삼중이제설의 중층적 논리 구조를 추출하고 결합하여 󰡔마조도일선사어록(馬祖道一禪師語錄)󰡕에 등장하는 “즉심즉불과 평상심”이 동일 논리 구조로 구성되었음을 논증하였다.󰡔중론(中論)󰡕의 ｢관열반품(觀涅槃品)｣에 등장하는 사구분별적 변증논법은 열반의 존재(A)와 비존재(not A)라는 두 대립명제를 바탕으로 인간이 사유할 수 있는 모든 판단인 사구를 설정하여, 열반이 존재와 비존재로 구성된 사구로 설명할 수 없는 중도(희론적멸)임을 천명하는 논법이다. 이 논법에 삼중이제설의 중층적 논리 구조와 결합하여 마조의 심(not A)과 불(A)로 이루어진 변증적 파기로 중도를 구현하는 방식의 선문답으로 계승된 것이다. 평상심 또한 시비, 취사 등의 사구분별로부터 해방된 중도이기에, 심과 불로 파기하여 드러난 대도체득과 다를 바 없고, 사구분별적 희론이 적멸한 열반이었다.본 연구를 통하여 마조의 “즉심즉불과 평상심”에 내재한 논리 구조가 인도고대논리학에 기반한 사구와 용수의 변증논법이 토대가 되었고, 이러한 사구분별적 변증논법과 삼중이제설의 중층적 변증논리가 결합하여 이루어졌음을 밝힘으로써, 마조선이 중국의 독자적 선이라는 인식에서 벗어나 인도선과 단절이 아닌 연속과 계승의 과정에 있음을 증명하고자 한다.
articles.abstract_en: This study analyzes the meaning of Mazu’s “The mind is the Buddha(卽心卽佛)” and “No-judgement Mind is The truth(平常心是道)” from the perspective of Prajñā-Madhyamaka Studies, based on the critical examination of “the perception that Mazu-Seon is an independently sinicized Seon beyond the Indian thought” and “the perception that ‘The mind is the Buddha’ is close to or equal to ‘No-judgement Mind’” interpreted by Yanagida Seizan and Iriya Yoshitaka. based on its perception. By analyzing out and combining Tetralemma’s dialectics of Nāgārjuna and multi level’s logical structure of ‘the theory of Two Truths in Three Steps(三重二諦說)’ of The Sanlun(三論學), it was demonstrated that the "The mind is Buddha and No-judgement Mind" in ‘Mazu yulu(A collection of Mazu’s sayings, 馬祖語錄)’ were described in the same logical structure.Tetralemma’s dialectic argumentation presented in the ‘The subject of Observation of Nirvana(觀涅槃品)’ of the “Mūlamadhyamaka-kārikā(中論)” is the idea that establishes all judgments that humans can think of, Four Phrases(四句), based on the two opposing propositions of Nirvana’s existence(A) and non-existence(not A), and proclaims that Nirvana is the middle way(=Prapañca’s Eternal Stopping, 戱論寂滅) that cannot be explained by Four Phrases(四句) consisted of existence(A) and non-existence(not A). Combined with multi level’s logical structure of the theory of Two Truths in Three Steps, it has been succeeded as the Seon Q&A(禪問答) in the way of realizing the middle way by dialectical destruction of Tetralemma of Mazo’s The mind (not A) and The buddha(A). Since No-judgement Mind is the middle way(中道) freed from Tetralemma of Right or Wrong(是非), Take or Leave(取捨), it is not different from Awaken the Truth(大道體得), which was destructed by The mind and The Buddha, and it is Nirvana where Prapañca Stops Eternally.Throughout this study, the logical structure which is inherent in “The mind is Buddha” and “No-judgement Mind” of Mazu was examined to be based on the dialectic of Nāgārjuna and Four Phrases(四句) on ancient Indian logic. By proving that it was made in combination with Tetralemma’s dialectic argumentation and multi level’s dialectic logic of the theory of Two Truths in Three Steps in Prajñā-Madhyamaka Studies, it confirms that Mazu-Seon thought has been in the process of continuation and succession, not disconnection from the Thought of Seon of the India, that is to say, it has been misunderstood that it is the independent Seon of the China.

articles.title_kr: 기후 위기 시대의 수행과 ‘나[我]’의 범주 확장 - 정토회의 ‘지속가능한 개발-부탄프로젝트’를 중심으로
articles.title_en: Practice in the Climate Crisis and the Expansion of the Concept of 'Self' : Focusing on the Jungto Society’s 'Sustainable Development Project' in Bhutan
articles.abstract_kr: This article begins with a contemplation on the role a practitioner can play, and the practices they might undertake, to address the severe climate crisis, which now seems almost irreversible. Recognizing that conventional practices alone may be insufficient to tackle this global-scale challenge, the article seeks to reassess the concepts and scope of practice, inspired by the life of the Buddha, who responded to the suffering of all beings with teachings of compassion.First, direction is sought from the Buddha's declaration to spread the Dharma, with form found in his daily practice, and the dynamics and manifestations examined within the tradition of the Sangha. Based on this, the concept and scope of practice are reevaluated by exploring examples where the agent and reach of practice have expanded. Consequently, although it is not an individual practice, Jungto Society's Sustainable Development Project in Bhutan falls within this redefined category of practice. This project explores whether the Buddha's life of simplicity and sufficiency can be realized on a national scale. In line with this vision, the people of Bhutan, with the support of the Jungto Society, have been actively engaged in pilot development projects since 2023.By analyzing this project, the text illuminates whether practice can extend beyond individual training to encompass social engagement initiatives and provide meaningful guidance for overcoming large-scale crises like the current climate emergency. It also explores what distinguishes this project from others, aiming to understand how the Buddha's teachings can be applied at a community level and what outcomes might be anticipated from such communal practice.

articles.title_kr: 일체지(자)의 직접지각론 __Pramāṇamīmāṃsā 1부 1장을 중심으로__
articles.title_en: The Direct Perception of Omniscient: Based on the Pramāṇamīmāṃsā 1.1
articles.abstract_kr: 인도인들은 전통적으로 인간에게 감각의 기능과 영역을 초월한 인식이 가능하다고 여겼다. 요가와 명상을 통해 수행자의 초월적인 직접지각(yogipratyakṣa)이 발생하기도 하는데, 이를 교주의 해탈지로 격상시켜 교리와 수행의 구심점으로 삼은 것은 자이나교와 불교였다.12세기 자이나 학승인 헤마짠드라는 전통과 당대의 인식논리학적 주제들을 망라하고자 총 5부의 Pramāṇamīmāṃsā(PM)를 구상했지만, 2부 1장의 미완으로 전해졌다. 본 고는 국내에 소개되지 않은 PM을 소개하고, PM의 직접지각론과 일체지를 고찰하며, 더 나아가 불교 요가행자의 증지와의 비교 연구의 토대를 제시하고자 한다.PM 1부 1장은 직접지각론으로 시작하는데, 이 중에서 영혼(jīva)의 본성이 발현되기 시작하는 최승 직접지각(mukhya pratyakṣa)이 설명된다. 최승 직접지각의 완성태인 일체지(sarvajñāna)는 이를 막는 4가지 유해업이 순수명상 2단계의 극점에서 모두 소멸할 때 현현한다. 그리고 이에 이르는 과정에서 물질적 대상을 투과하는 투시로서 초월지(avadhijnāna)와 심리적 대상을 투과하는 텔레파시로서의 타심지(manahparyāyajñāna)도 단계적으로 발현된다. 헤마짠드라는 자이나 전통의 일체지 인식론을 계승하면서도, 자신의 Yogaśāstra에서 상설(詳說)했던 명상론에 기반하여, 명상과 일체지의 관계를 밝혔다. 또한, 세간적 직접지각과 구분되는 최승 직접지각으로서 일체지에 도달하기까지 영혼의 정화 단계(구나스타나)에 따라 초월지와 타심지라는 인식을 밝힌 점도 특징적이다. 특히 자이나교의 최승 직접지각론은 실체적 대상들에 대한 영혼의 직접지각이라는 선명한 도식을 드러내는데, 이는 무아론에 기반하는 불교의 요가행자의 증지가 사성제를 대상으로 한다는 모호성과 대조적이어서 비교할 만하다.
articles.abstract_en: Traditionally, India has believed that human beings are capable of perception that transcends sensory functions and realms. Through yoga and meditation, practitioners can attain transcendent direct perception(yogipratyakṣa). Jainism and Buddhism, each in its own way, elevated the concept of transcendent perception to the level of spiritual liberation, making it a central tenet of their respective doctrines and practices.In the 12th century, the Jain monk Hemacandra attempted to encompass traditional and contemporary epistemological themes by conceptualizing a five-part Pramāṇamīmāṃsā(PM). However, the first chapter of the second part remains incomplete. This paper introduces the PM, which has not yet been explored in local scholarship. It examines Hemacandra's theory of direct perception and omniscience and lays the groundwork for a comparative study with Buddhist yogic realization.The first chapter of the PM begins with the theory of direct perception, explaining the supreme direct perception (mukhya pratyakṣa) in which the nature of the soul(jīva) begins to manifest. The culmination of this supreme direct perception is omniscience(sarvajñāna), which manifests when the four obstructive karmas are completely eradicated at the highest level of the second stage of pure meditation in Jain practice. In this process, transcendent knowledge (avadhijñāna), which penetrates material objects, and telepathy(manahparyāyajñāna), which penetrates psychological objects, are also progressively revealed.It is noteworthy that Hemacandra clarified the stages of the soul's purification, which lead to transcendent knowledge and telepathy, marking them as distinct from ordinary direct perception. These stages ultimately culminate in supreme direct perception and omniscience. The Jain doctrine of supreme direct perception(mukhyapratyakṣa) clearly presents a framework where the soul directly perceives substantial objects. In contrast, the Buddhist yogipratiyakṣa, based on the concept of no-self(anātma), targets the Four Noble Truths as non-discriminative knowledge, highlighting a distinct difference between the two.

articles.title_kr: ‘단순 비인식(adarśanamātra)’ 이론에 대한 다르마끼르띠의 비판 - 걜찹제의 『양평석의 해탈의 길을 밝힘』의 6가지 분류를 중심으로 -
articles.title_en: Dharmakīrti’s Critique of the Theory of Mere Non-Perception (adarśanamātra): Focusing on rGyal tshab rje’s Six-fold Systematization in rNm ’grel thar lam gsal byed
articles.abstract_kr: After Dignāga defined the three characteristics of valid inference, the method of establishing negative pervasion became a central issue in Buddhist logic. Īśvarasena argued that the third characteristic could be established through mere non-perception alone, but Dharmakīrti critiqued this as incompatible with Dignāga’s fundamental principles. This study clarifies the argumentative structure of PVI 16-20 using the six-fold classification presented in rGyal tshab rje’s rNam 'grel thar lam gsal byed as an analytical framework. Dharmakīrti's critique reveals that the theory of mere non-perception (1) renders the purpose of probative statements meaningless, (2) validates inferences that Dignāga rejected, and (3) permits even doubtful inferences. In particular, rGyal tshab rje presents original interpretations by reconstructing the opponent’s objections as logical dilemmas, refining the scope of application of Dignāga’s principles, and making implicit arguments explicit. This confirms that Dharmakīrti’s theory of essential relation is an ontological refinement of Dignāga's concept of ‘ascertainment’ and stands in continuity with Dignāga's thought.

articles.title_kr: 자이나교의 까르마론과 자유의지론 __영혼과 물질의 이항 대립과 초월의 구도__
articles.title_en: Theory of Karma and Free Will in Jainism: The Soul-Matter Dichotomy and Path to  Liberation
articles.abstract_kr: 고대 인도에서 윤회의 원인을 까르마로 지목하고, 이를 소멸하여 절대적 자유인 해탈로 지향하는 전통은 주로 슈라마나 종교에서 나타났다. 특히, 자이나교는 엄격한 결정론의 입장인 아지비까교와 심리적 의향이 우선적으로 고려되어야 한다는 불교의 동기주의적 입장과 대조적으로 물질적 까르마론에서 자유의지의 까르마 개념도 함께 제시하고 있어 흥미롭다.본 논문에서는 물질적인 까르마에 의해 그 결과가 산출된다는 업인업과의 입장에 있는 자이나교에서 누가, 어떻게 수행하여 까르마를 소멸하는지 제시하고, 더 나아가 이 수행을 가능케 하는 자유의지의 개념까지 소개한다. 이를 통해 영혼과 물질이라는 이항의 대립과 상호작용에 있어서 영혼이 물질을 초월해가는 구도를 살펴볼 수 있다.이에 Ⅱ장에서는 자이나교 해탈론의 구도와 해탈의 주체인 영혼의 특징을 소개하고, Ⅲ장에서는 영혼을 속박하는 물질적 까르마의 종류와 작용을 설명한다. Ⅳ장에서는 자이나교의 업장소멸의 고행론과 영혼의 정화단계에 따른 명상법을 정리하였다. 그 리고 Ⅴ장에서는 물질적 속박을 소멸하는 수행을 가능케하는 자유의지의 인자인 아디야바사야(adhyavasāya) 개념에 관해 고찰하고 그 의의를 제시하였다. 자이나교의 이 개념을 통해 영혼과 물질의 역동적이고 세밀한 길항 관계의 내부를 살펴볼 수 있으며, 자이나교의 까르마론이 결코 결정론이 아닌 자유의지론을 허용하고 장려하고 있음을 알 수 있다.
articles.abstract_en: In ancient India, the tradition that identified karma as the cause of saṃsāra (cycle of rebirth) and sought its annihilation to attain absolute freedom—mokṣa (liberation)—was primarily   found   within   the   Śramaṇa   tradition.   Notably, Jainism   presents   an   intriguing   contrast   to   other   contemporary schools: while the Ājīvika school adhered to strict determinism and Buddhism emphasized psychological motivation over material karma, Jainism introduced a concept of karma  that  incorporates  free  will  within  its  materialistic framework.This  paper  examines  how  Jainism,  which  upholds  the doctrine  of  action,  asserts  that  karma  produces  effects through  material  causes,  and  explores  who  can  eliminate karma  and  through  what  practices.  Furthermore,  it  introduces  the concept  of  free  will  that makes  such  ascetic practices  possible.  Through  this  analysis,  we  can  observe the dynamic interplay and opposition between soul (jīva) and matter (ajīva), wherein the soul gradually transcends material bondage.The structure of this paper is as follows: Chapter II introduces  the  framework  of  Jain  liberation  theory  and  the characteristics of the soul as the agent of liberation. Chapter III explains the types and functions of material karma that bind the soul. Chapter IV briefly outlines Jainism’s ascetic practices  for  the  destruction  of  karmic  residues  and  the meditative methods corresponding to the stages of the soul’s purification. Finally, Chapter V examines the concept of adhyavasāya (volitional determination) as the key factor of free will  that  enables  the  eradication  of  material  bondage  and discusses its significance.Through this concept, we gain insight into the intricate and  dynamic  antagonistic  relationship  between  soul  and matter  in  Jainism.  Moreover,  it  becomes  evident  that  Jain karma  theory  is  far  from  deterministic;  rather,  it  fundamentally accommodates a theory of free will.

articles.title_kr: 『사운다라난다』의 수행론 고찰 - 제12-15장을 중심으로 -
articles.title_en: The Structure of Buddhist Practice in Aśvaghoṣa's Saundarananda:  Focus on Chapters 12-15
articles.abstract_kr: This paper analyzes Cantos 12–15 of Aśvaghoṣa’s Sanskrit epic Saundarananda to reconstruct the regimen of Buddhist practice embedded in the poem and to assess its distinctive features and significance. Composed in Sanskrit and directed primarily to elite audiences such as Brahmins and the royal court, Saundarananda employs the Buddha’s direct sermons as a narrative vehicle, thereby transmitting practical instruction alongside literary artistry.After surveying prior scholarship, the study argues that these four cantos function not as mere literary ornament but as a set of systematic training modules. The section enumerates eight elements of practice that are well attested in early scriptures and in the Śrāvakabhūmi, yet Aśvaghoṣa re-orders them at the level of the sarga into a graded sequence: from initial resolve (entry into the path), through external cultivation (observance of precepts and restraint of the senses), through internal cultivation (moderation and energetic effort), culminating in samādhi.On this basis, three contributions emerge. First, by distributing the practice elements sarga by sarga, the poem offers a textbook-like, stepwise presentation of the path. Second, by embedding instruction within a persuasive narrative, it opens a plausible horizon of practice for lay readers and communicates doctrine compellingly to elite audiences. Third, while faithfully reflecting early Buddhist discipline, it simultaneously points toward continuities with later, Mahāyāna-oriented traditions of practice.

articles.title_kr: 차크라(Cakra/Chakra)를 둘러싼 리드비터(Leadbeater)와 우드로프(Woodroffe) 간의 논쟁점들에 대한 일고찰(Ⅰ) - The Chakras와 The Serpent Power를 중심으로 -
articles.title_en: A Study on the Points of Contention between Leadbeater and Woodroffe Regarding the Chakras (I):   Focusing on The Chakras and The Serpent Power
articles.abstract_kr: This paper examines three of the ten main points of contention between Leadbeater and Woodroffe regarding the chakras, along with one derived topic (a total of four issues), centered on Leadbeater’s The Chakras (hereafter Cks) and Woodroffe’s The Serpent Power (hereafter SP).The differences between the two figures and their works, which form the background of these debates, lie in the fact that Leadbeater, as a Theosophist, wrote Cks based on his clairvoyant observations of actual chakras through Theosophical practice and Theosophical philosophy. In contrast, Woodroffe, as a scholar of traditional Indian Tantra literature, authored SP by faithfully interpreting the chakras according to the textual tradition. Woodroffe criticized Leadbeater’s claims as deviating from traditional Indian thought.The four topics examined in order are as follows: ① The correspondence between the subtle bodies and sheaths: In traditional Indian thought, the prāṇic sheath is associated with the lower mind sheath, whereas in Theosophy, the etheric body (corresponding to the former) has no relation to the mental body (corresponding to the latter). ② The shape of the chakras: Leadbeater viewed them as convolvulus flowers, while Woodroffe saw them as lotuses(The form of the connection between the chakras and the spine: In Cks, the convolvulus flower is attached to a stalk extending from the spine, whereas in SP, the lotus is situated within the spine.) ③ The number of chakras: Leadbeater describes seven, while Woodroffe states six.As a result of studying these points of contention, it was found that although they appear similar on a macroscopic perspective, there are considerable differences in detail.

articles.title_kr: 내적 갈등 해소를 위한 불교 수행의 실천적 모색 - 초기불교 호흡관(Ānāpānasati)을 중심으로 -
articles.title_en: A Practical Exploration of Buddhist Meditation for Resolving Inner Conflict:  Focusing on the First Four Steps of Ānāpānasati in Early Buddhism
articles.abstract_kr: This study examines how individuals confronted with inner conflict may overcome suffering rooted in desire (abhijjhā) and discontent (domanassa). It argues that such afflictions can be resolved within the framework of concentration practice (samādhi), and identifies the first four steps of Early Buddhist mindfulness of breathing (ānāpānasati) as a preliminary practice optimized for this purpose. These initial steps are accessible to beginners regardless of circumstances, while also constituting a complete liberative framework described in the discourses as a “noble dwelling.” They further display a dual function, serving either as a basis for the four jhānas or as a foundation for insight practice through contemplation of impermanence, suffering, and non-self. The analysis suggests that concentration and insight operate in an integrated manner rather than as separate paths. By examining the usage and meanings of jhāna and its derivatives in the five Nikāyas and their commentaries, this study aims to clarify the Buddha’s approach to conflict resolution and contribute to reconstructing the original framework of Early Buddhist meditation, with particular emphasis on the practical role of the first four steps of mindfulness of breathing.

articles.title_kr: 찰나법연기의 자이나교 기원설
articles.title_en: Jain Origin Theory of the Momentary Dharma Theory on Conditioned Co-arising
articles.abstract_kr: 본 연구는 아비달마 불교의 찰나법연기(刹那法緣起) 설명이 초기불교보다 자이나교 철학에 더 큰 영향을 받았음을 주장한다. 찰나법연기설은 오랫 동안 불교의 고유한 이론으로 여겨졌으나, 로스팟(A. V. Rospatt)은 그 기원을 자이나교의 영향으로 추적한다. 찰나법연기설의 최초 흔적은 초기 경전이나 설일체유부(說一切有部)의 초기 문헌에서 발견되지 않으며, 기원후 2세기경  이후의『대비바사론』(大毘婆沙論)이나『아비달마구사론』(阿毘達 磨俱舍論, 4세기)에서 비로소 나타난다는 것이다. 반면에 자이나교 철학에 서는 업(業, karma)의 미세함(微, sūkṣma)을 설명하기 위해 원자적 시·공간 개념이 필요했다. 이에 따라 로스팟은 찰나법연기설이 자이나교의 영향을 받았을 가능성을 제기한 것이다. 본 연구는 각각의 철학적 체계들을 비 교 분석함으로써 로스팟의 주장을 지지한다. 초기 경전에서 연기, 12법, 연 기 공식은 하나의 체계이다. 연기는 범부가 스스로 구축한 인식과 존재의 틀 안에서 고통을 경험하는 과정을 드러낸다. 그 업 이론은 탐진치(貪瞋癡), 욕구, 지족, 고통 등을 바탕으로 한 업보론을 통해 삼계(三界, ti-dhātu)에 서의 생사·윤회를 설명한다. 반면, 아비달마에서 연기와 연기 공식은 찰나적으로 생멸하는 법들의 인연과 상속을 통해 모든 현상의 인과 관계를 설명하며, 십이연기는 ‘번뇌-업-재생’의 이중 구조로 삼세에 걸친 윤회를 설명한다. 이는 시간적 틀에서 [십이]연기를 형이상학적으로 설명한 것이다. 자이나교는 전생의 쾌락과 죄로 인해 업의 입자가 영혼(命我, jīva)으로 유입되고(漏, āsrāva) 속박되어(束縛, bandha) 재생이 이루어진다고 설명한다. 업의 미세함에 대한 설명은 공간적, 시간적 원자 개념을 요청하고 시간적 틀에서 ‘번뇌-업-재생’의 윤회관을 낳았다. 아비달마는 실체를 부정하지만, 원자론적 시간 개념을 통해 현상과 윤회를 설명한다는 점에서 자이나교와 유사한 사유 구조를 공유한다. 양자의 유사성을 토대로 본 연구는 ‘찰나법연기의 자이나교 기원설’을 주장한다.
articles.abstract_en: This  study  argues  that  the  momentary  dharma  theory on  conditioned  co-arising  in  Abhidharma  Buddhism  was more  greatly  influenced  by  Jain  philosophy  than  by  early Buddhism.  The  momentary  dharma  theory  on  conditioned co-arising  has  long  been  considered  a  unique  theory  of Buddhism, but A. V. Rospatt traces its origin to the influence of  Jainism.  The  earliest  traces  of  the  momentary  dharma theory  on  conditioned  co-arising  are  not  found  in  early scriptures or the early texts of the Sarvāstivāda school, but first appear in the Mahāvibhāṣā from around the 2nd century CE and the Abhidharmakośa from the 4th century. On the other hand, in Jain  philosophy, the concept of  atomic space  and  time  was  necessary  to  explain  the  subtlety (sūkṣma) of karma. For this reason, Rospatt suggested the possibility  that  the  momentary  dharma  theory  on  conditioned co-arising might have been influenced by Jainism. This study supports Rospatt’s claim by comparatively analyzing  the  philosophical  systems.  In  the  early  scriptures, conditioned co-arising, the 12 links, and the formula of conditioned co-arising are a single system. conditioned co-arising reveals the process by which ordinary people experience suffering within the framework of perception and existence they have constructed themselves. Its theory of karma explains  the  cycle  of  birth  and  death  in  the  three  realms (ti-dhātu) through a theory of karmic retribution based on greed, anger, ignorance, desire, contentment, suffering, and so  on.  In  contrast,  in  Abhidharma,  conditioned  co-arising and the formula of conditioned co-arising explain the causal relationships of all phenomena through the conditioning and continuity of momentarily arising and ceasing dharmas, and the 12 links explain the cycle of rebirth over three lifetimes as a dual structure of “defilement-karma-rebirth”. This is a metaphysical explanation of paṭiccasamuppāda within a temporal framework. Jainism explains that due to pleasure and sin from past lives, karmic particles flow into (āsrāva) the soul (jīva), are bound (bandha), and rebirth occurs. The explanation of the subtlety of karma requires spatial and temporal atomic concepts and gave rise to the view of rebirth as “defilement-karma-rebirth”  within  a  temporal  framework. Although Abhidharma denies substances, it shares a similar thought structure with Jainism in explaining phenomena and rebirth through an atomistic concept of time. Based on the similarities between the two, This study proposes the “Jain origin  theory  of  the  momentary  dharma  theory  on  conditioned co-arising”.

articles.title_kr: 밀교의 티베트 전래, 현밀 갈등과 그 대응:『보리도등론』의 교의적 특징과 문제점 고찰
articles.title_en: The Transmission of Tantric Buddhism to Tibet, the Exoteric-Esoteric Conflict, and Its Response: An Examination of the Doctrinal Characteristics and Issues in Bodhipathapradīpa
articles.abstract_kr: This paper analyzes the characteristics and limitations of tantric doctrine presented in Atiśa’s Bodhipathapradīpa, focusing on the doctrinal tensions between exoteric and esoteric Buddhism in India and Tibet. In the Bodhipathapradīpa, Atiśa places tantra (esoteric Buddhism) at the culmination of the Mahāyāna path, yet prohibits the bestowal of secret and wisdom initiations—which involve incompatible elements with monastic precepts—to ordained monks, and restricts his account on tantric attainments to worldly accomplishments. This approach makes tantric practice seem irrelevant to spiritual realization within the Bodhipathapradīpa alone.Nevertheless, a close investigation of Atiśa’s other works reveals that the ultimate goal of tantric practice is the attainment of wisdom and the buddhakāya. Yet, this higher spiritual realization presupposes the two prohibited initiations, as a result of which, a contradiction where ordained monks are excluded from attaining the very enlightenment that nessecitates these initiations, is created.Consequently, rather than a successful integration of the two, Bodhipathapradīpa can be understood as an imperfect but meaningful attempt to harmonize monastic discipline and tantric practice within the specific social and religious context of Tibetan Buddhism. Further research is needed to examine how these tensions were addressed in subsequent developments.

articles.title_kr: 바라와의 여래장 해석 연구 - 공성의 관점에서 해석된 여래장 고찰 -
articles.title_en: A Study of ’Ba’-ra-ba’s Interpretation of Buddha-Nature: An Examination of Buddha-Nature from the perspective of Emptiness
articles.abstract_kr: This paper focuses on the fact that ’Ba’-ra-ba rGyal-mtshan-dpal-bzang (1310–1391) identified himself as both a Māyopamādvayavādin (henceforth Illusionist) and a proponent of the *Svātantrika, and argues that the philosophical characteristics of the Illusionist tradition—namely, implicative negation (paryudāsapratiṣedha) and positive determination (pariccheda)—are applicable to his interpretation of Buddha-nature. This study addresses the issue of positive determination alongside an emptiness-based interpretation of tathāgatagarbha for two primary reasons: first, to avoid repeating general foundational matters covered in the author’s previous two studies; and second, to expand the discussion of tathāgatagarbha to the Illusionist tradition by examining emptiness (as implicative negation) in conjunction with positive determination. To this end, the paper first provides an overview of the Illusionist tradition in the introduction. The second chapter then examines Tsong-kha-pa’s (1357–1419) critique to explore the ideological characteristics of the Illusionists and the possibility of their connection to ’Ba’-ra-ba. Against this background, the paper analyzes ’Ba’-ra-ba’s interpretation of emptiness. ’Ba’-ra-ba regards the unconditioned (asaṃskṛta) tathāgatagarbha, separate from conventional phenomena, as the ground of all phenomena, and presents two types of emptiness corresponding to the two modes of reality/truth. These are the emptiness applied to the dharmadhātu and the emptiness applied to conventional phenomena. These forms of emptiness are implicative negation rather than non-implicative negation, implying through the negation of substantiality the affirmation of clarity (gsal ba) and cognition (rig pa), or conventional appearance. Therefore, ’Ba’-ra-ba’s interpretation of tathāgatagarbha can be understood from the perspective of emptiness as the “indivisibility of non-emptiness (=existence) and emptiness (=non-existence)” applied respectively to the two modes of reality/truth. Through this can one discern the point of convergence between the two correct views presented by ’Ba’-ra-ba: Madhyamaka and Mantrayāna.

articles.title_kr: 탈실체(無)와 드러남(有)의 무한: 안혜의『유식삼십송석(TrBh)』에 나타난 주체-의식의 역동성과 그 회귀
articles.title_en: The Infinity of Non-substantiality (無) and Manifestation (有): The Dynamics and Return of  Subject-Consciousness in Sthiramati’s Triṃśikāvijñaptibhāṣya
articles.abstract_kr: This paper examines the dynamic narrative of the religious-philosophical  “subject-consciousness  (vijñāna)”  as  it develops  toward  “non-substantiality  (無;  de-substantia)”  in Sthiramati’s  Triṃśikāvijñaptibhāṣya,    a  commentary  on Vasubandhu’s  Triṃśikākārikā . It  focuses  on  the  interplay between  this  movement  toward  emptiness  and  the  subsequent  “manifestation  (有;  Ereignis)”  from  that  place  of emptiness, which then reopens toward emptiness again.This  “subject-consciousness”  appears  in  the  mundane realm in verses 1 and 17 as “[continuous] transformation of consciousness  (vijñānapariṇāma)”  and  “[conceptual]  construction (vikalpa)” respectively. In the supramundane level of verses 26-30, it progressively de-substantiates into “[su-pramundane]  mind  (citta),”  ‘[refined]  knowledge  (jñāna),” “mind  free  from  [discrimination]  (acitta),”  sometimes  as “transcendental   knowledge  (jñānaṃ  lokottaram),” “uncontaminated realm (anāsrava dhātu),” “point of transformation of the subject (āśrayasya parāvṛtti),” and “thought free  from  [the  grasper]  (acintya).”  Ultimately,  this  process culminates in an ascending elevation that opens a new phase as the “body of liberation (vimuktikāya)” This does not represent an ontological perspective where the subject departs elsewhere, but rather signifies a philosophical position implying  the  transformation  of  subject-consciousness. Simultaneously,  it  demonstrates  the  religious  character  of Mahāyāna Buddhism, where the movement toward emptiness is linked to manifestation before again surging toward the journey of emptiness.Accordingly,  this  study  aims  to  elucidate—structurally, philosophically,    and    religiously    with    reverence—how Yogācāra thought understands the   practicing   subject through  the  transformation  of  ‘subject-consciousness’  as presented   in   Sthiramati’s  Triṃśikāvijñaptibhāṣya (TrBh), within the dynamic framework of ‘de-substantialization (無),’ ‘manifestation (有),’ and ‘return.’

articles.title_kr: 『사르바다르샤나상그라하』(Sarvadarśanasaṅgraha) 제13장 ｢빠니니다르샤나｣(Pāṇinidarśana)의 연구 (III) -마다바(Mādhava)가 논의한 다르샤나로서의 문법학-
articles.title_en: A Study of the Pāṇinidarśana Chapter  of the Sarvadarśanasaṅgraha (III): Vyākaraṇa (grammar) as a Darśana discussed by Mādhava
articles.abstract_kr: Grammar (vyākaraṇa), which started as one of the six important auxiliary Vedic disciplines (ṣaḍvedāṅga) along with phonetics (śikṣā), metre (chandas) and etymology (nirukta), in the morphological reconstruction work of reconstructing the padapāṭha text from the saṁhitāpāṭha text of the Rig Veda, later transcended schools and became the essential foundation (sarvapārṣadatva) for understanding all other disciplines. It further developed into a philosophical system (darśana) and came to be regarded as the royal road (rājapaddhati) to the ultimate goal of life (puruṣārtha).This paper examines Sāyaṇa Mādhava's discussion of grammar in Chapter 13, Pāṇinidarśana, of Sarvadarśanasaṅgraha, the only text that addresses grammar as a philosophy. In the first part, Mādhava primarily addresses morphological linguistics, including the meaning of "atha śabdānuśāsanam," morphology, and the purpose of grammar (vyākaraṇaprayojana). The middle section then devotes the lion's share of its discussion to sphoṭa.The purpose of this paper, the final in a series of studies on the Pāniṇidārṣāna, is to briefly introduce and critically examine the final part, which deals with the metaphysical linguistics of existence (sattā), universals (jāti) and individuals (dravya), and Brahman.

articles.title_kr: 후기 인도밀교의 제4관정(第四灌頂) 고찰:  아티샤의 관정론에 드러난 이제쌍입(二諦雙入)과 이타행(利他行)을 중심으로
articles.title_en: A Study of the Fourth Initiation (caturthābhiṣeka) in Later Indian Tantric Buddhism: Focusing on Atiśa's Theory of Initiation
articles.abstract_kr: This paper examines the long-standing problem surrounding the Fourth Initiation (caturthābhiṣeka) which is a culminating ritual in later Indian Tantric Buddhism. This initiation suffered from ambiguous definitions and purposes that caused diverse interpretations among various Buddhist traditions. The purpose of this paper is to analyze the unique initiation theory proposed by Atiśa Dīpaṃkaraśrījñāna (982~1054), by means of which his  philosophical value will be highlighted.Atiśa defined the Fourth Initiation as the ritual in which the master verbally transmits the ultimate state of the ‘Union (yuganaddha) of the Two Truths’ to the disciple. According to his doctrine, the achievement of this Union is intended to provide the epistemological and ontological premise for altruistic conduct by deliberately remaining in saṃsāra rather than abiding in nirvāṇa. This particular emphasis on altruistic conduct differentiates his stance from other interpretations on the Fourth Initiation, such as the Seven-Branch Yoga tradition, which focused on the representation of bliss and selflessness of phenomena, or the tenet of Pañcakrama, which concentrated on the thorough achievement and practice of non-dualistic wisdom.In conclusion, Atiśa’s doctrine on the Fourth Initiation demonstrates his philosophical endeavor. It was an attempt to reorient the trend of later Indian Tantric Buddhism, which often prioritized the realization of emptiness transcending dualistic thought, to the fundamental spirit of Mahāyāna Buddhism: the perfection of compassion and altruistic conduct.

articles.title_kr: 훈민정음 창제에 끼친 범어음성체계의 영향 연구 - 조선시대 『진언집』의 범자체계와 비교하여 -
articles.title_en: A Study on the Influence of the Sanskrit Phonological System on the Creation of Hunminjeongeum:  Compared with the Sanskrit System in the Joseon Dynasty's Jin-eon-jip
articles.abstract_kr: The creation of Hunminjeongeum by King Sejong stands as one of the greatest achievements in Korean history, yet the historical background surrounding its actual creation remains shrouded in mystery. This is because there are no prior records mentioning it before the 1443 December article announcing its creation. The specific phonetic principles and character creation methods of Hangeul were only detailed three years later, in 1446 September, with the publication of the Hunminjeongeum-Haerye. This paper examines how the phonetic principles and character creation methods of Hangeul's consonants and vowels, as presented in the Hunminjeongeum-Haerye, bear a significant resemblance to the grammatical system of Sanskrit, specifically through an analysis of the Jin-eon-jip (Collection of Mantras) transmitted during the Joseon Dynasty. This Jin-eon-jip reveals that its phonetic system is nearly identical to that of the Sil-dam-ja-gi, which was transmitted from China to Japan in the 8th century. This study examines the origin of Hangeul not through the perspective of character shape similarity, as previously mentioned in Korean linguistics history under the theory of Sanskrit origin, but through a comparative examination of the system of combining or articulating consonants and vowels as a writing system. Comparing the Sanskrit system in this Jin-eon-jip reveals that the phonological classification of consonants in Hangeul's 23 character chart - specifically the system of the molar sounds(牙音), lingual sounds(舌音), labial sounds(脣音), dental sounds(齒音) and throat sounds(喉音)—is nearly identical to the articulation of Sanskrit consonants, which follow the molar(牙), dental(齒), lingual(舌), throat(喉), labial(脣) sounds. Furthermore, the system of combining consonants and vowels as characters in Hangeul, or the system where the three elements—initial, medial, and final sounds—combine, is also closely related to the phonetic system of Sanskrit. Based on this examination, it is thought that the phonetic system of Sanskrit, transmitted through Buddhism, played a significant role in the creation of Hunminjeongeum. It is thought that when King Sejong was contemplating the creation of Hangeul, he received advice on the Sanskrit phonetic system, which was being transmitted by Buddhist monks like Sin-mi(信眉) etc, and thereby created the unique Hangeul script and linguistic system.

articles.title_kr: 해상 네트워크와 문화교섭의 상징세계 - 『삼국유사』의 허황옥·김수로와 『쿠쉬나메』의 아비틴·프라랑 서사 비교를 중심으로 -
articles.title_en: Maritime Networks and the Symbolic World of Cultural Mediation: A Comparative Study of the Narratives of Heo Hwang-ok and King Suro in the Samguk Yusa, and Abtin and Farāng in the Kush-nāmeh
articles.abstract_kr: This study explores the symbolic dimensions of maritime cultural negotiation reflected in two ancient intermarriage narratives: that of Heo Hwang-ok and King Kim Suro in the Samguk Yusa, and that of Abitin and Prarang in the Persian epic Kushnāmeh.Both stories, set against the vast maritime network connecting the Indian Ocean, the South China Sea, and the Korean Peninsula, articulate the themes of migration, union, and civilizational synthesis. Heo Hwang-ok’s journey from Ayuta to Gaya represents the reception of divine femininity and the legitimation of kingship, while Abitin’s exile from Persia and his union with a Silla princess symbolize the restoration of lost order through intercultural encounter.By analyzing these narratives in the context of maritime Silk Road exchanges and the Indian cultural worldview, this paper reveals how the sea functioned as a sacred and symbolic medium of transformation. These tales embody the memory of cross-civilizational exchanges that shaped the ancient Asian imagination, where the ocean served as both boundary and bridge.

articles.title_kr: 자이나교 칠구분별에서 ‘말할 수 없다’의 함의 - 불교의 사구분별과의 비교를 통해 -
articles.title_en: 'Avaktavya' in Jaina Sevenfold Predication:  A Comparison with the Buddhist Catuṣkoṭi
articles.abstract_kr: This paper examines the philosophical import of avaktavya (“inexpressible”) in the Jaina sevenfold predication (saptabhaṅgī), in comparison with the Buddhist four-cornered negation (catuṣkoṭi) and the notion of avyākṛta (“undeclared”). Through a close reading of key Jaina texts, the study shows that syāt functions not as a truth-functional operator but as a conditional marker (“from a certain standpoint”), and that avaktavya is not a confession of ignorance or a truth-value gap, but a normative device that enjoins the suspension of assertion when relevant conditions are not sufficiently specified. The seven predications are thus best understood as a family of regulated ways of speaking about a multi-aspectual reality, rather than as a list of seven distinct truth-values.Through a comparison with the Buddhist catuṣkoṭi and avyākṛta, the paper argues that the Buddhist scheme primarily serves as a reductio framework: it exhausts and dismantles all possible positions on a given statement, leading to the silence that points to emptiness and ultimate truth beyond words. By contrast, the Jaina saptabhaṅgī expands the space of conditional assertions under different standpoints (naya), conditions (catuṣṭaya), and the distinction between arpita and anarpita, seeking to capture as many partial truths as possible while avoiding overt contradiction.On this basis, the paper articulates the implications of avaktavya along four axes.First, on the epistemic and logical level, avaktavya expresses a normative suspension of judgment, an attitude of intellectual humility, and a recognition that truth is grasped through a plurality of partial standpoints.Second, on the ontological level, it completes anekāntavāda by allowing permanence and impermanence, existence and non-existence, to be affirmed together under different conditions without collapsing into trivial contradiction.Third, on the soteriological level, it marks the gap between the cognition of the bound soul and that of the liberated kevalin, and indicates that certain experiences—such as omniscience or deep samādhi—can be lived yet resist full verbal articulation.Finally, on the ethical level, avaktavya extends ahiṃsā to the domains of speech and belief by discouraging dogmatic assertion and harmful language, thereby contributing to the minimization of karmic bondage through disciplined assertion. In this sense, avaktavya is not merely a logical curiosity but a cross-sectional concept linking Jaina logic, metaphysics, soteriology, and ethics.

articles.title_kr: 두땅가(dhutaṅga, 頭陀行)의 본질에 대한 해석  –마하위하라파와 아바야기리파의 견해 비교–
articles.title_en: The Interpretation of the Nature of Dhutaṅga  — A Comparative Study of the Views of Mahāvihāra and Abhayagiri —
articles.abstract_kr: This paper examines how Mahāvihāra and Abhayagiri in Theravāda Buddhism understand and interpret dhutaṅga, one of the Buddhist practices, by focusing on their representative texts, Visuddhimagga and Vimuttimagga.Mahāvihāra defines dhutaṅga as both the cause that brings about the elimination of defilements (kilesa) and the possession of dhamma that eliminates them. They understand the intention (cetanā) accompanying this dhamma as the essence of dhutaṅga and classify it as paramattha. On the other hand, Abhayagiri regards dhutaṅga either as the thirteen dhutaṅga items or as their practice, and understands it as paññatti because its nature is neither wholesome (kusala) nor unwholesome (akusala) and is determined by the practitioner's state of mind. Mahāvihāra criticizes Abhayagiri on the grounds that something nonexistent, such as paññatti, cannot remove defilements. However, Abhayagiri also asserts that the dhutadhammas—namely alobha and amoha—function to eliminate defilements, which renders Mahāvihāra’s critique less persuasive.Meanwhile, both agree that unwholesome dhutaṅga cannot exist. However, based on their shared recognition that dhutaṅga is influenced by the practitioner’s state of mind, they diverge: Abhayagiri understands it as a paññatti, which cannot be categorized as wholesome or unwholesome, whereas Mahāvihāra regards it as paramattha, of which the essence lies in a wholesome intention. Given that dhutaṅga is a practice rooted in voluntary choice, Mahāvihāra emphasizes the intention that is the fundamental motivation for practice, while Abhayagiri focuses on the practice itself, highlighting a key difference in interpretive approach between the two traditions.

articles.title_kr: 즈냐나가르바의 저작 『이제분별론』의  논쟁사적 맥락 읽기 - 『이제분별론』의 첨가 게송 37-43을 중심으로 -
articles.title_en: Reading the Madhyamaka-Yogācāra Conflicts in Jñānagarbha’s *Satyadvayavibhaṅga
articles.abstract_kr: This paper examines the *Satyadvayavibhaṅga (bDen pa gnyis rnam par 'byed pa) of Jñānagarbha, an eighth-century Madhyamaka philosopher, focusing on the antaraślokas 37-43. Those verses are considered in terms of the history of Madhyamaka-Yogācāra conflicts in reference to Śāntarakṣita’s (725-788) commentary, the *Satyadvayavibhaṅgapañjikā. The verses under consideration contain a debate between the Yogācāras and the Mādhyamikas that presupposes Dharmapāla’s (530-561) critique of Bhāviveka (500-570) and the critique of the Madhyamaka definition of ‘conventional reality’ (saṃvṛti-satya) by the early commentators of Dharmakīrti’s (600-660) Pramāṇavārttka, namely, Devendrabuddhi (630-690) and Śākyabuddhi (660-720). The paper, as a whole, emphasizes that Jñānagarbha’s *Satyadvayavibhaṅga invites further research aiming to illuminate, not only the history of the conflicts between Madhyamaka and Yogācāra, but how the Mādhyamikas expressed their truth claims after Dharmakīrti’s innovation of the Yogācāra philosophy.

articles.title_kr: 중국과 인도의 우주본체론 비교 고찰 - 『태극도설』과 SāṃkhyaKārikā 의 전변설을 중심으로 -
articles.title_en: A Comparative Study of Chinese and  Indian Cosmological Ontology
articles.abstract_kr: 본고는 신유학의 기원인 『태극도설』과 상키야 철학의 고전인 SāṃkhyaKārikā(SK)에 나타난 전변설을 비교분석하며, 중국과 인도의 우주본체론이 인간의 행동과 사회에서 다르게 표출되는 과정을 밝히는 작업이다. 『태극도설』은 ‘무극·태극’이라는 일원적 우주본체로부터 ‘음양·오행’을 거쳐 만물이 생성되는 과정을 보여준다. 이는 ‘천인합 일’이라는 중국 전통철학의 고유한 사유형식을 반영하며, 인간은 우주본체의 이치를 사회 속에서 실천하는 성인을 이상으로 삼게 한다. SK는 뿌루샤와 쁘라끄리띠의 이원 적 전변설을 주장한다. 두 전변설의 차이는 인간의 행동과 사회에서 구체적으로 드러 난다. 본고는 이를 ‘원형적 세계관’의 관점에서 고찰한다. ‘원형적 세계관’은 개별 현상 의 근원이 되는 원형(原型)을 심상적 직관으로 인식하고, 그 원형을 통해 세계를 이해하 는 관점이다.중국과 인도는 모두 순환·반복의 세계관을 공유하지만, 중국은 일회적 생사관인 혼 백설을 토대로 세밀한 역사 기록과 사회질서 유지를 통해 우주본체의 이치를 현실에 구현하려 했다. 반면에 인도는 반복적 생사관 안에서 해탈이라는 궁극적 목표를 설정 하였다. 전통과 사회질서에서도 중국은 우주본체 안에서 조화를 이루는 구심력의 문 화라면, 인도는 개인이 해탈을 추구하는 원심력과 기존 사회질서를 유지하려는 구심 력이 이중적으로 공존하는 문화이다.
articles.abstract_en: This paper compares and analyzes the theory of universal transformation (pariṇāma) presented in the Taijitu Shuo (Diagram of the Supreme Ultimate Explained), the origin of Neo-Confucianism, and the SāṃkhyaKārikā (SK), a classic of Sāṃkhya philosophy. It elucidates how the cosmological ontologies of China and India manifest differently in human behavior and society. The Taijitu Shuo demonstrates the process by which all things are generated from the monistic cosmic principle of ‘Wuji and Taiji’ through ‘Yin-Yang and the Five Elements’. This reflects the unique mode of thought inherent in traditional Chinese philosophy, ‘the unity of heaven and humanity’, and establishes the sage — who practices the principles of the cosmic essence within society — as the ideal. SK advocates the dualistic theory of transformation involving Puruṣa and Prakṛti. The  difference  between  these  two  theories  of  transformation  manifests concretely in human actions and society. This paper examines this from the perspective  of  an  ‘archetypal  worldview’,  which  refers  to  the  mode  of understanding the world through original archetypes intuitively perceived as the source of individual phenomena. While both China and India share a cyclical, repetitive worldview, China sought to embody the principles of the cosmic  essence  in  reality  through  meticulous  historical  records  and  the maintenance of social order, based on the non-cyclical (once-occurring) view of life and death (hun-bai). In contrast, India set the ultimate goal of liberation (mokṣa) within its cyclical view of life and death. In terms of tradition and social order, China represents a centripetal culture that seeks harmony within the framework of the cosmic essence, while India embodies a dualistic culture in which two opposing forces coexist: the centrifugal drive of individuals pursuing liberation, and the centripetal effort to maintain the existing social order.

articles.title_kr: 『마하바라타』 지옥 서사의 구조와  윤리적 기능
articles.title_en: The Structure and Ethical Function of the Hell Narrative in the Mahābhārata
articles.abstract_kr: 본 연구는 『마하바라타』 제18권에 나타나는 지옥 서사를 분석하여, 이 장면이 카르마 의 인과법칙을 확증하는 교리적 공간이 아니라 다르마의 윤리적 의미를 재구성하는 서사적 장치로 기능함을 밝히는 것을 목적으로 한다. 기존 연구는 이 서사를 후대 힌 두교 문헌에서 체계화되는 응보적 지옥 관념의 전조로 이해해 왔다. 그러나 본고는 유 디슈티라의 지옥 체험을 중심으로 서사를 재검토함으로써, 해당 장면이 특정 죄와 형 벌의 대응 관계로 조직된 교리적 설명이라기보다 전통적인 권선징악의 도식을 의도적 으로 전복하는 서사적 장치임을 논증한다. 특히 의로운 왕 유디슈티라가 지옥에 이르 고, 반대로 악의 상징인 두료다나가 천상에 거하는 가치 전도는 업보에 따른 보상 논 리를 흔들며 강렬한 윤리적 긴장을 형성한다. 나아가 유디슈티라가 지옥에서 고통받 는 존재들과 함께 머물기를 선택하는 장면은 다르마의 근거가 외적 상벌 질서가 아니 라 타자의 고통에 응답하는 자비의 감응에 있음을 시사한다. 이러한 분석을 통해 본 연구는 『마하바라타』의 지옥 서사가 응보적 정의의 단순한 재현을 넘어, 전쟁 이후의 윤리적 책임과 기억을 성찰하게 만드는 서사적 장치이며 다르마의 의미를 인간적 감 응성의 차원에서 재사유하도록 하는 핵심 장면임을 제시한다.
articles.abstract_en: This study argues that the hell narrative in Book 18 of the Mahābhārata does not function as a doctrinal confirmation of karmic retribution but as a narrative device that reconfigures the ethical meaning of dharma. Previous scholarship has often treated the epic’s hell as a precursor to the systematic models of retribution found in later Hindu traditions. Yet Yudhiṣṭhira’s experience in hell reveals a different logic. The episode disrupts the conventional scheme of rewarding virtue and punishing vice: the righteous Yudhiṣṭhira encounters hell, while Duryodhana appears in heaven. This inversion destabilizes the notion of karmic compensation and generates a profound ethical tension within the narrative. Yudhiṣṭhira’s decision to remain with the suffering foregrounds compassionate responsiveness (dayā, 慈悲) rather than reward and punishment as the ground of dharma. In this way, the hell episode prompts a reconsideration of dharma - not as a system of moral recompense, but as an ethical responsibility emerging from compassion in the aftermath of war.

articles.title_kr: 인도 불교식 결혼 의례의 변화 양상과 그 함의 -2000년대 초반 이후 마하라슈뜨라 서부 지역을 중심으로-
articles.title_en: Transformations in Buddhist Wedding Rituals in India: Western Maharashtra since the Early 2000s
articles.abstract_kr: 이 연구는 인도 마하라슈뜨라 서부 지역의 불교도 공동체에서 행해지는 결혼 의례의 변화 양상을 분석하고 그 사회·문화적 함의를 고찰하는 것을 목적으로 한다. 연구는 먼저 문헌 자료를 통해 불교식 결혼 의례의 형성 배경을 검토한 후, 2001~2003년 사 이 필자가 현지에서 참여 관찰한 네 건의 결혼식과 2021~2025년 사이 유튜브에 공개 된 결혼식 영상 다섯 건을 비교 분석하였다.분석 결과, 삼귀의와 오계의 독송, 망갈 숫따의 낭송, 신랑·신부의 결혼 서약, 화환 교 환과 망갈수뜨라 수여 등은 두 시기에 공통적으로 나타나는 핵심 요소로서 불교도 결 혼 의례의 기본 구조를 형성하고 있었다. 그러나 최근의 결혼 의례에서는 다양한 경전 독송, 가족 참여 확대, 반지나 꽃다발 교환 등 새로운 요소가 추가되며 의례의 절차가 전반적으로 확대되고 복잡해지는 경향이 나타났다. 또한 일부 사례에서는 띠까나 신 두르와 같은 힌두교적 상징이 등장하는 반면, 암베드까르가 결혼 의례의 핵심으로 제 시했던 물단지와 흰 실 의례가 생략되는 경우도 확인되었다.이러한 변화는 불교 공동체가 힌두교 중심적인 문화 환경, 미디어 환경의 변화, 그리 고 사회·경제적 성장 속에서 결혼 의례를 지속적으로 재구성하고 있음을 보여준다. 불교식 결혼 의례는 단순한 종교 의례를 넘어 공동체의 정체성을 표현하고 재확인하 는 문화적 실천으로 기능하고 있다.
articles.abstract_en: This study examines the transformation of Buddhist wedding rituals among Neo-Buddhist  communities  in  western  Maharashtra,  India.  It  begins  by reviewing the textual and historical foundations of these rituals, focusing on B.R. Ambedkar’s guidelines that delineate the fundamental elements of a Buddhist marriage ceremony. The research employs a comparative analysis of four wedding ceremonies observed through field participation between 2001 and 2003, and five subsequent ceremonies conducted between 2021 and 2025, analyzed via online video recordings.The findings indicate that core ritualistic components  ―  including the recitation of the Three Refuges and Five Precepts, the chanting of the Maṅgal Sutta, the exchange of vows and garlands, and the presentation of the mangalsutra ― have remained consistent across both periods. However, contemporary ceremonies exhibit increased complexity, characterized by expanded scriptural recitations,  enhanced  familial  participation,  and  the  introduction  of  new symbolic items such as rings and bouquets. Notably, while some ceremonies incorporate Hindu-derived elements like tilak or sindoor, the “water-pot and white-thread” ritual prescribed by Ambedkar is occasionally omitted. These shifts suggest that Buddhist wedding rituals are being continuously reshaped by evolving social, cultural, and media environments, even as they remain a vital expression of community identity.

articles.title_kr: 자비심의 심소적 해석에 대한 고찰 - 안혜의 『유식삼십송석』을 중심으로 -
articles.title_en: A Study on the Yogācāra Interpretation  of Compassion(Maitrī-karuṇā ) - Focusing on Sthiramati’s Triṃśikāvijñaptibhāṣya  -
articles.abstract_kr: 본 연구는 자비심에 대한 초기불교의 해석이 어떠한지 살펴보고, 유식 심소의 분류 체 계에서는 어떻게 설명이 되고 있는지 안혜의 『유식삼십송석』을 중심으로 살펴본다. 자비심은 불교의 핵심 교의로서 초기불교의 자비관 수행과 사무량심에서 중요한 위치 를 차지하며, 유식학에서는 선심소로 분류된다.안혜는 자비심을 무진(無瞋) 심소와 불해(不害) 심소로 체계화하였다. 무진은 진(瞋)의 대 치로서 자심(慈心, maitrī)에 해당하며, 중생에게 즐거움을 주는 실천이다. 불해는 해(害)의 대치로서 비심(悲心, karuṇā)에 해당한다. 안혜는 비심을 세 차원에서 해명하였다. 어원 적으로 ‘[자신의] 행복을 제거한다’는 의미이다. 즉 타자의 행복 상실을 포착하는 인식으 로부터 시작하여 자신의 아만심의 만족을 제거하는 의미에서 행복의 제거한다는 뜻한 다. 정서적으로 타인의 고통을 함께 느끼는 공감적 아픔이고, 실천적으로 해치지 않는 비폭력의 행위이다.유식의 심소 분류 체계에서 진은 근본번뇌이며 해는 수번뇌이다.초기불교는 다른 양상을 보인다. 『수타니파타』 「자경」에서 자심은 여락과 불해를 포괄 하는 통합적 개념이며, 『맛지마 니까야』의 사무량심은 자심과 비심의 기능을 구분한 다. 네 가지 무량심이 유기적으로 연결된 통합적 수행 체계로 제시된다.본 연구를 통해 초기불교의 통합적 자비관이 유식학에서 무진과 불해로 분석되어 정 밀한 심리학적 체계로 발전하였음을 확인하였다. 안혜의 해석은 비심의 어원 분석과 정서·실천 차원의 통합을 통해 연민의 본질을 깊이 해명하였다는 독창성을 지닌다.
articles.abstract_en: This study examines the interpretations of compassion (maitrī-karuṇā) in Early Buddhism and investigates how it is explained within the classification system of mental factors (caitta)  in Yogācāra, focusing specifically on Sthiramati’s Triṃśikāvijñaptibhāṣya. As a core tenet of Buddhism, compassion occupies a vital position in the cultivation of Buddhist loving-kindness and the four immeasurables  (apramāṇa)  of  Early  Buddhism,  and  it  is  categorized  as  a wholesome mental factor (kuśala-caitta)  in Yogācāra philosophy. Sthiramati systematizes compassion into two mental factors: non-hatred(adveṣa) and non- harming(avihiṃsā). Non-hatred corresponds to loving-kindness(maitrī)  as the practice of bringing happiness(yogarakṣaṇa), while non-harming corresponds to compassion(karuṇā)   as  the  practice  of  removing  suffering(duḥkhaprahāṇa). Notably, Sthiramati provides an original interpretation of compassion through etymological, affective, and practical dimensions. However, early Buddhist compassion presents loving-kindness as an integrated concept encompassing non-harming,  and  the  four  immeasurables  emphasize  organic  connection rather  than  hierarchy.   This  reveals  how  early  Buddhism's  integrated understanding of compassion developed into Yogācāra's precise psychological analytical system.

articles.title_kr: Yogācāra Curriculum for Five Fields of Science
articles.abstract_kr: The  Yogācārabhūmi  introduces  and  justifies  five  fields  of  science, pañcavidyāsthāna, which are learning the Buddha’s speech, grammar, medicine, logic, and the mundane arts and crafts. In the Bodhisattvabhūmi chapter, it is stated that Boddhisattvas, who aim not only to attain their own liberation but also to rescue suffering beings, should learn all five subjects. The examination of relevant texts demonstrates that this Bodhisattva idea reflects a change in the ideal type of Buddhist practitioner. An early Buddhist text, the Suttanipāta, regards ideal Buddhists as those who concentrate on their own spiritual cultivation and do not pay attention to learning medicine, ritual formulae, and the interpretation of signs, which are not directly related to Buddha’s teachings. In a later Mahāyāna text, however, knowledge beyond the Buddha’s own teachings was regarded as useful for helping other beings, which would in turn increase faith in Buddhism. Therefore, the establishment of five sciences can be regarded as a phenomenon corresponding to the emphasis on altruism, which is ultimately connected to proselytization, within the Buddhist tradition.

16권 호.abstract_kr: The purpose of this study is to examine ‘the view of selfness in the Sāṁkhya’. The manifested world arising from three constitutions(triguṇa) having discerned essentially as the misery, the Sāṁkhya think to annihilate the misery. As the triguṇa being the constitutions of the prakṛti of physical reality in nature consist in pleasure, pain and illusure etc., so they produce necessarily to the misery. Due to this reason, we experinces the varied pains in the physical and psychological aspcets. The impulses of the pain suffered by us influence further the psychological sides rather than the physical one. Because the physical aspects are momentary while the psychological one should remain eternally as long as they are located in the bondage. Therefore though the whole of evolutes manifested from triguṇa belong to the empirical self, of these the empirical self being limited to the internal organs, I will examine for the purpose of the relationship between the Spiritual principle(puruṣa) and the internal organs(antaḥkaraṇa).

The Attendant Aasanas of Classical Yoga
17권 호.abstract_kr: The other attendant āsanas preceded by the four fundamental āsanas have a common point showing more relaxed mode than the latter. The other attendant āsanas are distinguished mainly by a mode of folding or stretching legs.The steadiness leads the comfortableness properly among fundamental āsanas, while the comfortableness leads the steadiness properly among the other attendant āsanas. The steadiness required in āsanas is to aim at concentrated meditation after all, and it needs the comfortableness for this aim.Patañjali says in Yogasūtra(Ⅱ.47), “[Āsana are perfected] by relaxation of effort and by attaining oneness in meditation with the infinite.” This instruction is to elucidate the principle of āsanas again. In this case, we can understand that ‘relaxation of effort’ means the comfortableness, and that ‘attaining oneness in meditation with the infinite’ means the steadiness. As explained in Yogasūtra-bhāṣya, just a āsana that leads to mental concentration by relaxation of effort is a perfected āsana intended in classical yoga. Just here is a turning point where āsanas are divided into Rāja-yoga and Haṭha-yoga.Peculiar āsanas of Haṭha-yoga substitute stiffness for steadiness i.e. effort, and relaxation for comfortableness. However repeated training of both stiffness and relaxation is effective in order to maintain āsanas of classical yoga requiring steadiness and comfortableness. Therefore from this point of view, when āsanas of Haṭha-yoga become the process of matching steadiness and comfortableness, they are recognized as valuable means for classical yoga.

Raamaanuja's Criticism of 'Sa'nkara's Theory of Avidyaa
17권 호.abstract_kr: Examination of other viewpoints is as necessary as exposition of one's own viewpoint. Rāmānuja(1017-1137), a leading theistic Vedāntin, is at his best not only in elucidating the Viśiṣṭādvaita philosophy, but also in examining the views of others in general and Advaita philosophy in particular.Avidyā which is otherwise called māyā is the key concept through which Advaita works out its metaphysics, epistemology, and ethical discipline. The distinction between nirguṇa-Brahman and saguṇa-Brahman presupposes the concept of avidyā. Further, In the system of Advaita, just as the difference between Brahman and jīva is the work of avidyā, even so the pluralistic universe is a product of avidyā. In the same way, the subject-object epistemology involving the distinction of the knower, the known, and the resulting knowledge and the theory of vivarta in terms of which the problem of error is sought to be explained presuppose the concept of avidyā.The Advaita theory of avidya is not acceptable to Rāmānuja. Considering that the concept of avidya plays an important role in Advaita, it is necessary for Rāmānuja to examine this concept carefully and formulate his objections against it. This is in the mahāasiddhānta of the Śrī-bhāṣya, i.1.1. He raises seven major objections, what is called saptavidha-anupapatti, against the Advaita theory of avidyā.I propose to consider in this paper the meaning of saptavidha-anupapatti and the manner in which Ramanuja in his Śrī-bhāṣya criticizes the Advaita theory of Avidyā.

17권 호.abstract_kr: The recognition of the Nāgārjuna’s nirvāṇa does not to recognize the essential śūnyatā which deny the saṁsāra of the birth-death, but insight to the essential śūnyatā in the recognition of the saṁsāra. In this meaning, the recognition of the Nāgārjuna’s nirvāṇa is the saṁsāra of the birth-death, but it has a thorough practicality of the śūnyatā as a pratītyasamutpāda.The relation between the saṁsāra and the nirvāṇa in the Nāgārjuna’s thought is a co-relation of the thorough negation and affirmation. In this point, Nāgārjuna’s thought consists in the middle position which is not a being or not a nothing. Accordingly, it also means which is not insist on an individual particular opinion. Also it means to confirm all opinions as it is.So Nāgārjuna refutes the Sarvāstivādin’s a substantial thought of the nirvāṇa, and then he re-interprets the world of the nirvāṇa on the pratītyasamutpāda-niḥsvabhāva-śūnyatā. He will establishes to practice the ultimate goal of the nirvāṇa in the mundane world. It is a view of Nāgārjuna’s the nirvāṇa on tmadhyamāpratipad in the Madhyamaka-Kārikā.

The Survey of the Methodology of 'Sa'nkara's Advaita Philosophy
17권 호.abstract_kr: The purport of this article consists in bringing to light by analyzing the structure of dual meaning of the “Advaita” dictum, through what methodology Śaṅkara developed the absolutistic monism of the Upaniṣads. As a result, it becomes intelligible that the Advaita(non-duality) may mean that the appearing world is not existent independently of Brahman, as well as that the subject and the object are not distinct, and logically the former presupposes the latter.In this article, it becomes understandable that Śaṅkara admitted a large part of the philosophy of his teachers's teacher Gauḍapāda. It shows that although Śaṅkara tried to dissociate the Buddhistic philosophical traits from Gauḍapāda's philosophy which is largely influenced by Vijñānavāda and Śūnyavāda, his own philosophy remains with Buddhistic influence. His methodology through which he made an attempt to approach the Absolute, Oneness of the individual self and the Reality by starting from the level of empirical cognition invested with the subject-object duality represents this fact. In addition, through the culture-philosophical consideration of the historical background of the formation of Śaṅkara's philosophy it becomes intelligible that his Advaita philosophy is the concrete amalgam of the philosophical stream from the Vedic thought including Upaniṣads through Buddha's philosophy to Gauḍapāda's philosophy, a learned man of Vijñānavāda and Śūnyavāda.

17권 호.title_en: The Survey of the Methodology of Sankara`s Advaita Philosophy
The Method of 'Continuity and Discontinuity'(anvayavyatireka) in 'Sa'nkara and Sure'svara
17권 호.abstract_kr: Advaita Vedānta is a system of philosophy in which the revelation-oriented attitude is highly valued although the significance of reasoning has never been forgotten. Early Advaitins such as Śaṅkara, Sureśvara make use of the method of anvayavyatireka which is nothing but a reasoning so that the meaning of mahāvākya (great saying) of the Upaniṣads can be revealed in terms of the identity of Ātman and Brahman. The method is basically related to the discrimination(viveka) between what is continued present and what is absent.For Śaṅkara and Sureśvara the method of anvayavyatireka is employed to know the meaning of the word like tvam (you) and aham (I) in the mahāvākya for understanding the whole sentence. To know what the word tvam really stands for it is necessary to grasp the fact or reality of all the terms (things) that indicate it. The Self exists continuously in the waking, dreaming, and sleeping state, but on the contrary, the non-Selves such as body (deha), ego (ahaṃkāra), intellect (buddhi), which are superimposed on the Self, cannot exist continuously since they are present in some state and are absent in other state. As a result the Self is discriminated from the non-Selves through this reasoning and a foundation is made for further apprehension of the complete sentence.The method of anvayavyatireka is a pure reasoning based on experience without any metaphysical basis. It is by this method that the revelation of the Upaniṣads is to be reinforced and the reasoning itself to be fulfilled in its own sphere.

19권 호.abstract_kr: The concept of yoga represents the core of Indian spiritual sādhana.Generally the technical meaning of yoga is a concentration, and yoga is the process of mental discipline that is common to all Hindu sects. And most of all the Hindu systems including the Nyāya, Vaiśeṣika, Sāṃkhya, Yoga and Vedānta Darśana accept the utility and relevance of yoga in their respective systems.In Jaina philosophy, the term of yoga has many-sided meaning. In this paper, the writer studies the various instance and meaning of yoga in Jaina literature.The writer says that there are fundamental differences with the Hindu yoga. And she points out that the word of yoga is mainly used in the sense of activities of kāya, manas, and vacana in Jaina philosophy.In a general way, it is said that Jaina tradition predominantly lays stress upon austerities, tapas.For all that, the writer comments that the samyak cāritra, right conduct of tri-ratna is the exact equivalent of the general term ‘yoga sādhana’, and Jaina yogic sādhana consists of dravya sādhana and bhāva sādhana. Dravya sādhana, the external sādhana equals to tapas and bhāva sādhana, the internal sādhana means to meditation.And the writer points out that Jainism lays stress upon meditation more than tapas.In Jaina meditaion, especially the kāyotsarga is not merely a yogic posture, it is a state of mind of one which pursuing the spiritual goal. It is the most important item in Jaina yoga.By practicing the meditation, the sādhaka can purify his soul from karmic pudgala. And it leads one to mokṣa.The Jaina yogic sādhana is neither difficult nor arduous. It is very easy to learn, easy to practice, easy to accept, easy to master skillful.
19권 호.abstract_en: 자이나교에서의 요가 개념은 다른 인도 철학파의 용법과 달리 매우 다양하다. 특히 요가라는 말이 카르마 이론과 관련되어 보다 먼저, 널리 사용되었기 때문에 수행론상의 용례가 두루 쓰이지 않게 되었다고 본다.그리고 자이나교에서 요가라는 말은 사다나의 일부를 이루고 있다고 보아야 하며, 고행과 명상이라는 두 부류의 수행 방법으로서 구체화되어 있다는 점을 2종의 요가 사다나라는 체계를 통해서 고찰하고 있다.특히, 3보 중 정행을 이루는 요가 사다나가 고행과 명상이라는 해명을 통해서, 그 중 일부인 고행에만 너무 치중하여 자이나교의 사다나를 바라보는 편향된 관점에는 보다 균형적인 시각이 필요하다는 논지를 전개하고 있다.또한 자이나 명상 요가의 체계를 카욧사르가의 3종 자세와 2단계를 중심으로 하여 도표로 정리한 뒤 설명을 덧붙이고 있다.

19권 호.title_en: The debate on activities(k？ritra) in the Sarv？stiv？da system
19권 호.abstract_kr: It is generally said that, Within the Sarvāstivāda ontological system, there requires a distinction between two theories: the existence of all dharmas in the three time periods and the existence of the intrinsic nature (svabhāva) of dharma in the three time periods.The former has been traditionally demonstrated from the four proofs, the two proofs taken from hearing from others (sūtra) and the two proofs based on inference (anumāna) presented at the Abhidharmakośabhāṣya, while the letter has been insisted from the four theories fomulated by the four Sarvāstivāda masters, Dharmatrāta, Ghoṣaka, Vasumitra, and Buddhadeva, since the Mahāvibhāṣāśāstra. The theory of activities (kāritra) seems to be the core theory which link the two ontological theories mentioned above.For the Sarvāstivādins, it is possible through the theory of activities (kāritra) that past, present, and future time is distinguished and the activities of dharmas, arising, duration, decay and ceasing, is explained. According to the theory, a past dharma is one whose activities have been cease to exist, a present dharma is one whose activities are operating, and a future dharma is one whose activities hava not operated yet. What changes momentarily is not the intrinsic nature (svabhāva) of a dharma but its activities through the inherent characteristic (svalakṣaṇa).There still are problems involved in the activities of visual organ, the present tat-sabhāga, along with the relationship between past sabhāgahetu and present niṣyandaphala. Saṅgabhadra seems to solve this problem through introducing the concept of capability (vyāpāra) into the Sarvāstivāda ontological system.
19권 호.abstract_en: 유부 존재론은 ‘三世實有法恒有’로 정의된다. 그리고 이 명제의 근거는 雜阿含經에 나와 있는 二經二敎證을 통해서 알 수 있다. 그러나 이것은 삼세실유의 근거는 되지만, 법체항유의 근거는 되지 않는다. 법체항유는 大毘婆舍論에서의 4대논사의 說을 계기로 성립되었다고 볼 수 있다. 따라서 유부의 실유사상은 二經二理證에 의해서 삼세실유를 주장하고, 그 논리적 귀결로 법체항유를 이론적으로 확립했다고 할 수 있다. 그리고 이 ‘삼세실유·법체항유’의 상호관계를 뒷받침하는 것은 세우(Vasumitra)의 位不同說(avasthanyathika)에 따른 作用論이다. 그러나 이러한 유부의 작용론은 ‘피동분(tat-sabhga)의 눈’이나 ‘과거 동류인(sabhga-hetu)’ 등의 문제로 인해, 세친에 의해 철저히 비판 받는다. 이에 중현은 세친의 비판을 작용(kritra) 이외에 공능(vypra)의 개념을 들어 반론한다. 따라서 본 논문은 유부 작용론을 둘러싼 세친과 중현의 논쟁을 통해, 유부 작용론의 의미를 검토했다.

21권 호.title_kr: 『根本說一切有部毘奈耶雜事』의 勝鬘(Mallikā) 이야기를 통해 본 여성의 이미지 분석
21권 호.title_en: An analysis on the image of women in the Mallikāvadāna of the Mūlasarvāstivādavinaya Kṣudrakavastu
21권 호.abstract_kr: Malli or Mallikā is one of still very popular female names in India. As in the other Indian religious traditions, in the Buddhist tradition also, a woman named Mallikā appears. This paper deals with Mallikā story of the Mūlasarvāstivādavinaya Kṣudrakavastu where it performs not only the structural and sociohistorical analysis but also highlights the Mūlasarvāstivādins' view of women in this story.Mallikā’s episode presents the Mūlasarāvstivādins’ rich literary imagination as an Indian version of the Cinderella story. This is an example of the combination between Buddhism, Indo-european mythology and local tradition. The Mallikā story represents the strong desire for social upgrade from the lower class of Indian society. The episode of Mallikā and Varṣikā represents the social situation of that time: the harmony between wives and their paying respect to their husband were regarded as essential to the family. The analysis of this episode reveals that women are content with a passive status in a male dominant society. This reflects the inclinations of the avadānas of the MSV to reconcile with social custom. Mallikā’s giving birth to Virūḍhaka is the beginning of the main episode of the Śākyas’ massacre by Virūḍhaka. Here arises the question: why did the Mūlasarāvstivādins connect Mallikā, symbol of good deeds, and Virūḍhaka, symbol of bad deeds? The MSVKv does not provide any karmic explanation. Just like the slave-girl who gives birth to Pūrṇa and is never mentioned again in the Pūrṇāvadāna, another avadāna of the MSV, following the birth of Virūḍhaka, Mallikā is briefly mentioned in the scene of the meeting with Prasenajit after she was driven from the palace. Through a similar process, the slave-girl gives birth to Pūrṇa who becomes a disciple of the Buddha whereas Mallikā’s son, Virūḍhaka takes part in a massacre. This is the Mūlasarāvstivādins’ method of creating stories. They do not consider the karmic relation between the protagonists and their mothers. Mallikā, a doer of good deeds through past and present, is even ousted from the palace by her own son. This also reflects the Mūlasarvāstivādin’ view of women which could not but be influenced by the social realities of their time when women were subordinate to men. In many cases, women are secondary characters who only introduce the male protagonists and as shown in the table 6 and the past story of Mallikā, they are often described as worldly obstacles to the male protagonists’ enlightenment.

21권 호.abstract_kr: The 'Three Characters(trairūpya) of Reason(Hetu)' is a very important notion in Buddhist Logic which typically shown with Three-step arguments. This theory of 'Three Characters of Reason' is systematized by Dignaga, Buddhist Logician, and perfectly completed by Dharmakīrti. The Buddhist logic which it is completed by Dharmakīrti gave much influence to the later Mādhyamikas in Indian Buddhism. Among the later Mādhyamikas, Śāntarakṣita is one of most famous for succeeding inBuddhist Logic and Buddhist essential thoughts. In Madhyamakālaṃkāra-vṛtti, his famous work, he make an effort to demonstrate Buddhist essential thought, i.e. the niḥsvabhāva or anātma in the world, by means of Logic and Āgama. Specially on the part of Logic, Śāntarakṣita adopts and uses the reason of Ekānekasvabhāvaviyoga, the famous theory of reason, and explains the reason according to the 'Three Characters of Reason' in Buddhist logic. In considering the Śāntarakṣita's explaining, we make an notice to the influence of Dharmakīrti and Bhāvaviveka who is a middle Mādhyamika. Therefore we reach to know that Śāntarakṣita is succeeded in Buddhist Logic and previous Mādhyamika. Notwithstanding such an influence, Śāntarakṣita is unique for demonstrating Buddhist essential thought with reason of Ekānekasvabhāvaviyoga.
21권 호.abstract_en: 〔주요어: 이일다성, 증인, 삼상, 중관장엄론, 샨타라크쉬타, 다르마키르티〕인의 삼상이란 종인유로 구성되는 삼지작법으로 대표되는 불교 논리학에서 이유인 원인의 특성을 보여주는 중요한 개념이다. 이에 대한 설명은 디그나가에 의해 체계화되고 다르마키르티에 이르러 정교하게 된다. 후기 중관학파의 논사 가운데 다르마키르티의 논리학을 전승한 대표적인 인물인 샨타라크쉬타는 중관장엄론에서 불교의 근본적인 특성인 무자성, 무아의 개념을 논리에 의한 증명과 성전에 의한 증명으로 논증하고 있다. 특히 논리에 의한 증명에서 그는 유명한 이일다성의 증인을 이유로 하여 무자성의 논증을 전개한다. 그의 논리학적 전개는 다르마키르티의 인의 삼상론에 의거하고 있으며, 또한 중기 중관학파의 논사인 바바비베카의 영향도 크게 받고 있다. 곧 샨타라크쉬타는 이일다성의 증인의 이유를 전개함에 있어 ‘승의에 있어서’라는 한정을 붙이며, 원인으로서 이유는 그와 유사한 동품에 반드시 존재하며, 그리고 원인과 전혀 별개의 이품에는 이유는 존재하지 않는 것을 논증하고 있다.샨타라크쉬타의 이일다성의 증인은 후대 인도불교사에서 무자성을 논증하는 대표적이며 독특한 성격, 그리고 이전의 다양한 불교적 특성을 보여 주는 중요한 논증식으로 간주되고 있다.

0권 23호.abstract_en: 반야심경은 대승불교, 특히 반야사상의 핵심을 담고 있는 경전이다. 그리고 반야사상은 반야심경의 주제인 반야바라밀이라는 개념을 통해서 구현된다. 이러한 반야바라밀의 이해에 있어서 하나의 관건이 되는 문제가 반야바라밀과 반야바라밀다呪의 관계이다.이 글에서는 반야바라밀자주를 다루는 인도주석가들의 관점을 살펴봄으로써 하나의 시사를 얻고자 하였다. 현재 그들의 梵本 주석서는 전하지 않고 있으나, 티벳 역본이 전하고 있는 주석가는 모두 8인이다. Donald S. Lopez Jr.에 의한 영역을 저본으로 하여, 8인의 주석가들의 관점을 반야심경 전체에 대한 평가가 반영된 科目의 관점을 살펴 본 뒤에, 다시 본문해석(隨文釋)에 나타난 관점을 살펴보는 방법을 취하였다.그 결과 만트라 부분이 갖는 독자적 의의를 인정하지 않는 顯敎적 이해방식과 독자적 의의를 인정하는 ‘밀교’적 이해방식의 두 가지로 나눌 수 있었다. ‘密敎’적 이해 방식 안에는 밀교뿐만 아니라 명상 내지 禪的 차원에서 이해하는 것까지를 함께 포괄하여 묶어 보았다. 그것은 공히 언어 밖의 차원을 인정함으로써 顯敎적 이해방식과는 다른 것으로 평가되었기 때문이다.
